operator_io_quirks: Tiny DB: Person=4 rows, PersonFriend=4 rows; read_schema sampling is trivial, no huge-table path exercised.
Person.name is varchar(20) PRIMARY KEY but declared NOT NULL=0; sqlite PK implies uniqueness but not NOT NULL in this DDL text.
PersonFriend has NO primary key (pk=[]); sample_fresh_primary_keys must handle empty PK (no dedup) without crashing.
PersonFriend has TWO FKs both to Person(name): name->Person.name and friend->Person.name; both must be filled from Person's final name column.
Self-ish structure: PersonFriend.name and .friend both reference the same parent column; FK fill draws with replacement from Person.name (4 values).
Column named 'year' (INTEGER) in PersonFriend: extract_typed_values replaces whole-word 'year' with placeholder before parsing; must strip placeholderrare and still map to column YEAR.
Column named 'name' appears in both tables; literal pool anchoring by column name will hit both Person.name and PersonFriend.name (and FK-root to Person.name).
Declared types: varchar(20) -> String fuzzer (char family, length=20); INTEGER -> Number; TEXT -> String (char family, length default 20).
No mixed-case/spaced identifiers here; all names simple ASCII, but keep double-quoting anyway.
Storage classes match declared types (text/integer); no contradicting storage.
No NULLs in original (null_rate 0.0 everywhere) but NOT NULL not declared, so TS may emit NULLs via empty-parent FK path only if parent empty (it won't be).
PersonFriend.year values are small ints (5,6,10,12) — Number fuzzer with scale from INTEGER (no args) will produce wide-range ints, not year-like.
operator_ts_expectations: Person.name: String fuzzer, length range from elements (4-5 chars) up to 20; fresh random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() plus contamination; PK single-column -> max_l0=inf so many fresh draws.
Person.age: Number fuzzer, INTEGER no args -> scale 0, range [-1,1] roughly (10^0), perturbed by +-1/+-2; will produce tiny ints unlike 25-45 originals.
Person.city: String fuzzer; fresh random strings dominate, original city names only via 5-element sample; likely FN on city predicates.
Person.gender: String fuzzer with only 2 distinct elements; p=0.2 fresh strings will inject implausible genders -> FN on gender='male'/'female'.
Person.job: String fuzzer, 3 distinct; same implausibility risk.
PersonFriend.name/friend: FK fill from Person.name final values (4 names) with replacement -> duplicates and ties likely; good for FP on join/group-by ties.
PersonFriend.year: Number fuzzer INTEGER -> tiny ints near 0, not 5-12; predicates like year>10 may flip.
PersonFriend has no PK so no PK dedup; duplicate (name,friend,year) rows possible -> ties/duplicates present, may cause FP on DISTINCT-less queries.
FK fill uses replacement so PersonFriend rows may repeat same friend many times -> cardinality skew vs original 4 distinct.
String contamination (suffix/prefix/drop char) on names may break equality joins between Person.name and PersonFriend.name? No — FK fill copies exact parent values, so joins hold.
Number fuzzer list_max quirk: with 4 elements, list range upper overwritten to full-range max (1), so fresh ints cluster near 0.
Date/Time/Bool fuzzers unused (no such declared types).
